title: Two Exceptional-Point Regimes in the Spinterface Model of Chirality-Induced Spin Selectivity
abstract: The spinterface model of chirality-induced spin selectivity supports two algebraically distinct near-exceptional-point (EP) regimes, which cannot be mixed. A \emph{gold-level} near-EP involves the two gold spin states under an anti-Hermitian, electrode-mediated spin flip with spin-symmetric dissipative broadening (Scheme~B). A \emph{chain-level} near-EP involves the collective coalescence of the two molecular eigenstates with largest weight on the first molecular site under a Hermitian on-site Rashba spin flip with spin-dependent broadening (Scheme~A). Mixing the diagonal cancellation of one scheme with the off-diagonal structure of the other yields a strictly negative discriminant and admits no EP on any parameter path, making the gold/chain classification exhaustive. At the gold near-EP the spin-flip coupling is chirality-selective, converting achiral spin-valve transport into purely chiral transport across well-defined crossover points. At the chain near-EP the Petermann factor grows as a power law in chain length, with an exponent tunable by the Rashba coherence length and non-monotonic in the Rashba strength, reflecting a balance between coherent enhancement and progressive breakdown of the Scheme-A condition. Both near-EPs are dressed versions of the ideal two-state EP, and the ratio between observed and bare EP locations measures the delocalisation of the coalescing pair, providing a fit-free diagnostic of the mechanism. These results identify CISS junctions as a solid-state platform for non-Hermitian spectral physics.
summary: This work analyzes the spinterface model for CISS, identifying two distinct, non-mixable near-Exceptional Point (EP) regimes. By using the NEGF formalism, the authors demonstrate that these EPs manifest as unique signatures in spin-selective transport and power-law scaling of the Petermann factor. The findings establish CISS junctions as a promising solid-state platform for non-Hermitian physics.
main_problem: The paper investigates the behavior of chirality-induced spin selectivity (CISS) when the effective non-Hermitian Hamiltonian becomes singular, corresponding to an Exceptional Point (EP). It focuses on classifying and characterizing two distinct, non-mixable near-EP regimes.
main_result: The model supports two distinct near-EP regimes—a 'gold-level' (Scheme B) and a 'chain-level' (Scheme A)—which are physically separated by an algebraic obstruction. These EPs provide a solid-state platform for studying non-Hermitian spectral physics.
method: The analysis uses the Non-Equilibrium Green's Function (NEGF) framework to derive an effective non-Hermitian Hamiltonian. Key diagnostics include analyzing the Petermann factor scaling and comparing observed EP locations to bare theoretical predictions.
model_or_system: The system is the spinterface model applied to molecular junctions, involving a central molecular region coupled to leads (gold site and molecular chain). The Hamiltonian incorporates molecular hopping, electrode coupling, and spin-orbit/exchange interactions.
key_observables: Chirality-selective transport (conversion from achiral to purely chiral), the Petermann factor ($K_k$), and the ratio between observed and bare EP locations.
important_parameters: Rashba coherence length ($\lambda_R$), chain length ($L$), and the specific conditions defining the two schemes (Scheme A: Hermitian, Scheme B: Anti-Hermitian).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the NEGF formalism and the assumption that the two EP regimes are algebraically distinct and cannot be mixed.
figures_summary: The notes reference figures showing the $L$-dependent effective splitting of the Petermann factor, illustrating collective scaling and the crossover between different physical regimes.
paper_structure: The paper develops the full Hamiltonian using NEGF, derives the effective non-Hermitian Hamiltonian, identifies the conditions for the two distinct EP schemes (A and B), and then analyzes the resulting transport signatures, including scaling laws and crossover points.
why_interesting: The explicit connection between topological features (EPs) in non-Hermitian physics and measurable transport phenomena (chirality-selective spin filtering) provides a concrete, solid-state platform for testing advanced quantum theories.
